annotations.text:
Pick a direction before we build the rest.

Each board is the same product page — the screen that carries the hardest job on this site: telling someone a garment is genuinely one-of-a-kind without turning it into a pressure tactic.

Same product, same price, same 15-minute hold, same facts. Only the voice changes.

A — ATELIER

Gallery hush. Big uninterrupted imagery, Bodoni display, cool paper neutrals. The piece is treated as a catalogued object.

For: makes ordinary stock look considered; ages well.
Against: slower to scan; can read as expensive and standoffish.

B — BAZAAR

Aubergine and gold, full-bleed imagery, a struck seal for the one-of-one. Closest to the feeling of the shop itself.

For: warm, unmistakably Indian, memorable.
Against: a strong ground competes with the garments — needs disciplined photography to work.

C — REGISTER

The catalogue as an archive. Hairline rules, tabular data, piece and lot numbers on show. Stock reads "1 — the only one" as a plain record line.

For: the honest one; scarcity is a fact in a table, never a nudge. Fast to scan, and it is literally true to how the stock is held.
Against: unromantic; risks underselling the clothes.
